title: Tenerife
blurb: Practical things to know before (and while) you visit Tenerife: places, food, beaches, trips, the language and island life.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the Canary Islands?
questions.fact: Menorca is in the Balearic Islands. The Canaries lie in the Atlantic, off the coast of north-west Africa.

questions.q: What is the biggest of the Canary Islands?
questions.fact: Tenerife covers roughly 2,000 square kilometres and is the most visited of the islands.

questions.q: Roughly how far is Tenerife from the African coast?
questions.fact: That is close enough for the Saharan dust wind, the 'calima', to reach it now and then.

questions.q: What is the capital of Tenerife?
questions.fact: It is a port city on the north-east coast and shares the title of Canary Islands capital with Las Palmas on Gran Canaria.

questions.q: About how high is Mount Teide, the highest peak in Spain?
questions.fact: It is the third-tallest volcano in the world measured from the sea floor.

questions.q: What sort of mountain is Teide?
questions.fact: Teide is still classed as active, though it has been quiet for a long time.

questions.q: When did Tenerife last have a volcanic eruption?
questions.fact: The Chinyero eruption was in 1909. The 2021 eruption was on La Palma, another Canary island.

questions.q: What is the airport code of Tenerife South (Reina Sofía), where most holidaymakers land?
questions.fact: TFN is Tenerife North (Los Rodeos), mostly used for inter-island flights.

questions.q: How long does a transfer from Tenerife South airport to Playa de las Américas usually take?
a: About two and a half hours
questions.fact: Resorts in the south are close to the airport. Getting to the north takes longer.

questions.q: Ferries to La Gomera leave from which port?
questions.fact: The crossing takes about 50 minutes to an hour, and you can often spot dolphins and whales.

questions.q: What is the island's public bus company called?
questions.fact: Its green buses are called 'guaguas'. A tram also runs between Santa Cruz and La Laguna.

questions.q: Which two places does Tenerife's tram connect?
a: Puerto de la Cruz and La Orotava
questions.fact: It is the only tram line on the island and is handy if you stay in the capital area.

questions.q: Which way do you go round a roundabout in Tenerife?
a: Whichever direction is quickest for you
Straight across the middle if it's empty
Clockwise, just like roundabouts in the UK
questions.fact: Drive on the right and give way to traffic already on the roundabout.

questions.q: What is the legal drink-drive limit for most drivers in Spain?
questions.fact: That is lower than the limit in England, so the safe choice is not to drink if you are driving.

questions.q: UK visitors: what do you need for the sockets in Tenerife (pictured)?
a: A transformer to step the power up a lot
Nothing at all, UK plugs fit directly
A plug adaptor; the voltage is the same
A voltage converter for 110 volt devices
questions.fact: Spain uses two round pins (types C and F) at 230 V.

questions.q: This clock shows 3pm in London on a summer day. What time is it in Tenerife?
a: 5pm, two hours ahead of the UK
4pm, one hour ahead of the UK
questions.fact: The Canaries use Western European Time, the same clock as the UK all year, and they change the clocks on the same dates.

questions.q: The Canary Islands charge which sales tax instead of Spain's mainland VAT?
questions.fact: The general rate is only 7%, which is why perfume, electronics and some other goods can be cheaper than at home.

questions.q: What is the usual tip in a restaurant in Tenerife?
a: A fixed €10 per table, whatever you eat
At least 20% of the total bill
Not required; round up or leave 5 to 10%
Tipping is considered rude on the islands
questions.fact: Service is rarely added to the bill, so a few euros for good service is appreciated.

questions.q: Which number do you call in an emergency in Tenerife?
questions.fact: 112 works anywhere in the EU, and operators usually speak English.

questions.q: UK visitors: which card can give access to Spanish state healthcare, alongside travel insurance?
questions.fact: A GHIC doesn't replace travel insurance. Check the rules before you travel.

questions.q: Why might small shops be shut in the afternoon?
a: They only open when a cruise ship is in port
They close for a mid-afternoon break (siesta)
They shut whenever the sun gets too hot
It is a public holiday every afternoon
questions.fact: Resort shops stay open, but in smaller towns hours can be split.

questions.q: When do local families usually eat dinner?
questions.fact: Restaurants in tourist areas open earlier, but you'll find the locals arrive later.

questions.q: How much colder than the coast can it be at the top of Mount Teide?
a: About the same as at the coast
questions.fact: Take a jacket, sunglasses and water, and expect the air to be thin.

questions.q: What is the 'calima'?
a: A tide that comes in very fast
A hot, dusty wind from the Sahara
A sudden evening thunderstorm in summer
A winter mist that rolls onto the coast
questions.fact: It brings haze and higher temperatures for a few days, and can be hard on people with breathing problems.

questions.q: What is the 'mar de nubes' (sea of clouds)?
a: A sandstorm that blows across the sea from Africa
A giant wave that floods the southern beaches
A thick fog that covers the whole island day and night
A cloud layer below Teide while the summit is sunny
questions.fact: Climb above the clouds and the sky can be bright blue.

questions.q: Which side of Tenerife is usually sunnier and drier?
questions.fact: The south sits in the rain shadow of the mountains, which is why most resorts are there.

questions.q: Why is the north of Tenerife so much greener?
a: It receives all of the island's volcanic soil
Trade winds drop their rain on the northern slopes
The ocean is much warmer on that side
Farmers there water it from the island's only big river
questions.fact: Look out for laurel forests and banana plantations in the north.

questions.q: About how warm is the sea around Tenerife in January?
questions.fact: It is refreshing rather than warm. The sea reaches 22 to 23°C in late summer.

questions.q: Which months are usually the hottest in Tenerife?
questions.fact: Even then, the coastal temperatures are usually 26 to 30°C, not extreme.

questions.q: What does 'La cuenta, por favor' ask for?
questions.fact: A very useful phrase at the end of a meal.

questions.q: What does 'cerrado' on a shop door mean?
questions.fact: 'Abierto' means open.

questions.q: What does 'tirar' on a door mean?
questions.fact: 'Empujar' means push.

questions.q: What do you get if you ask for 'una caña' in a bar?
a: A fishing rod for the harbour
A black coffee with a little sugar
A small glass of draught beer
questions.fact: 'Una caña' is the standard way to order a small beer in Spain.

questions.q: What is a 'tinto de verano'?
a: Red wine with fizzy lemonade, served cold
A fruit punch served in a big jug
A heavy red wine from the volcanic vineyards of Tenerife
A rum cocktail with fruit and mint
questions.fact: Its name means 'red wine of summer'.

questions.q: What does 'agua sin gas' mean?
questions.fact: 'Con gas' is sparkling.

questions.q: What does 'peligro' on a sign mean?
questions.fact: You might see it by cliffs, on rough paths and near the sea.

questions.q: What does 'prohibido el paso' mean?
questions.fact: 'Prohibido' means forbidden.

questions.q: What does '¿Habla inglés?' mean?
a: Can I have the bill, please?
questions.fact: Most people in resorts will say yes, and appreciate you trying a little Spanish.

questions.q: When someone says 'gracias', what do you reply with 'de nada'?
questions.fact: A friendly reply to 'thank you'.

questions.q: What do you do when you say '¡Salud!'?
a: Say cheers when raising a glass
Say sorry for bumping into someone
Greet someone first thing in the morning
Ask the waiter for the bill
questions.fact: It literally means 'health'.

questions.q: What do Canarians call a bus?
questions.fact: A Canarian word. On mainland Spain it is an 'autobús'.

questions.q: In the Canaries, what are 'papas'?
questions.fact: On mainland Spain they say 'patatas'.

questions.q: What does 'un café cortado' get you?
a: Strong coffee with a splash of milk
An iced coffee with ice cream on top
A coffee with a shot of liqueur
questions.fact: 'Cortado' means 'cut' with milk.

questions.q: What are papas arrugadas?
a: Crispy fried chips with paprika and salt
Thin potato crisps sold in packets in every bar and kiosk
Small potatoes boiled in salty water until wrinkled
Mashed potato topped with grated cheese
questions.fact: They are eaten skin and all, usually with mojo sauce.

questions.q: The red and green sauces served with papas arrugadas are called what?
questions.fact: Red mojo (rojo) is spicy and made with paprika. Green mojo (verde) is made with coriander or parsley.

questions.q: What is gofio?
a: A soft goat's cheese that is made on the island
A hearty fish stew with potatoes
Toasted cereal flour, a traditional staple
A sweet banana liqueur from the north
questions.fact: Canarians have been eating it since before the Spanish arrived.

questions.q: What is 'queso asado'?
a: A thick cheese soup served in a bowl
Grilled cheese, often served with mojo
A sweet cheese dessert with honey on top
Cheese wrapped in bacon and deep-fried
questions.fact: Goat's cheese is typical. It's a good vegetarian starter.

questions.q: What is 'conejo en salmorejo'?
a: Rabbit in a garlicky, spiced marinade
Chicken in an almond cream sauce
Fish in a spicy tomato and pepper broth
Pork with pineapple and a rum sauce
questions.fact: A classic Canarian dish, often served with papas arrugadas.

questions.q: What is 'ropa vieja' in the Canaries?
a: A stew of chickpeas, meat and vegetables
A second-hand clothes market in Santa Cruz
A sweet dessert made with banana and rum
A cold potato salad with tuna and egg
questions.fact: The name means 'old clothes'.

questions.q: Which fish is a Canarian favourite, usually grilled whole?
a: Trout from the island's mountain streams
questions.fact: Ask for the 'pescado del día' (fish of the day).

questions.q: Which Tenerife drink is this layered coffee?
questions.fact: It has condensed milk, liqueur, coffee, milk and a dusting of cinnamon.

questions.q: What is 'leche y leche'?
a: Two glasses of cold milk side by side
Coffee with condensed milk and milk
A tall glass of milk with a banana
Tea with milk and a spoon of honey
questions.fact: A sweet coffee that is typical of the Canary Islands.

questions.q: What is 'ron miel'?
questions.fact: A sweet local spirit often served as a digestif.

questions.q: On which island is Dorada beer brewed?
questions.fact: Tropical is Gran Canaria's beer.

questions.q: Canarian bananas are known for being...?
a: Seedless and sour like a lemon
Larger and greener than imported ones
questions.fact: Look for the label 'plátano de Canarias'.

questions.q: What is a 'guachinche'?
a: A small mountain refuge where walkers can sleep and eat
A small family-run place with home-made wine and food
A traditional craft market in the north
A small fishing boat used in the harbours
questions.fact: Most are in the north. They are cheap, and some open only for a few months.

questions.q: What is a 'menú del día'?
a: A day trip by coach to Teide
A daily bus pass for tourists
The weather forecast for the day
questions.fact: Often two or three courses with a drink, and good value.

questions.q: What is 'bienmesabe'?
a: A spicy red sauce for fish
A banana liqueur from La Palma
questions.fact: The name means 'tastes good to me'.

questions.q: Which is one of Tenerife's official wine regions?
questions.fact: Tenerife has several designated wine regions, and grapes grow on volcanic soil.

questions.q: What is a 'ración' on a menu?
a: A dessert that comes with coffee
A small free snack with a drink
A set meal for one person
questions.fact: A tapa is smaller. Raciones are good for the whole table.

questions.q: What is 'sancocho canario'?
a: A sweet cake made with gofio and honey
Salted fish stew with potatoes and mojo
A sweet banana pie with cream on top
A cold tomato and onion salad with olives and tuna
questions.fact: Traditionally made with salted fish.

questions.q: Why is the sand golden at Playa de las Teresitas near Santa Cruz?
a: It is crushed seashells from the coast
It is volcanic ash ground very fine
It was shipped in from the Sahara
It was dredged up from the sea bed
questions.fact: Most natural beaches in Tenerife have dark volcanic sand.

questions.q: A red flag is flying at a Tenerife beach. What does it mean?
a: Dangerous conditions: stay out of the water
Lifeguards are on duty and you can swim anywhere freely
It is a dog-friendly beach today
questions.fact: Atlantic currents and waves can be strong. Flags are there for a reason.

questions.q: A yellow flag is flying at the beach. What does it usually mean?
a: The beach is closed because of sharks
Take extra care, conditions are moderate
Sharks have been seen close to the shore today
Sunbeds are free for everyone today
questions.fact: Green means safe and red means danger.

questions.q: Which animals live all year in the channel between Tenerife and La Gomera?
a: Blue whales feeding in deep water
Orcas that follow the fishing boats
questions.fact: Boat trips from the south coast often see them, as well as bottlenose dolphins.

questions.q: Who designed the sea-water swimming complex Lago Martiánez in Puerto de la Cruz?
questions.fact: He was a Lanzarote artist who shaped much of the Canary Islands' look.

questions.q: Which bay near Costa Adeje is known for turtles?
questions.fact: Please don't touch or chase the turtles.

questions.q: If you get caught in a strong current when swimming, what is the best advice?
a: Swim straight back against the current as fast as you can
Dive underwater and hold on tight
Stay still and shout for help
Swim parallel to the shore, then back in
questions.fact: Raise an arm and signal for help if you're tired.

questions.q: Which south-coast resort is famous for its nightlife and the 'Veronicas' strip?
a: Los Gigantes, below the big cliffs
Puerto de la Cruz in the north
questions.fact: It's busy until the early hours. For something calmer, try Costa Adeje or Los Cristianos.

questions.q: Which southern resort is a working fishing port and ferry harbour, popular with families?
questions.fact: It has a sheltered beach and boat trips.

questions.q: Which resort area is known as the more upmarket part of the south-west coast?
questions.fact: Playa del Duque is its smart beach.

questions.q: Which north-coast resort has a botanical garden founded in the 1700s?
a: El Médano, in the south east
Costa Adeje, in the south west
questions.fact: It is one of Tenerife's oldest tourist towns, and quite different from the southern resorts.

questions.q: Which resort sits beneath huge sea cliffs on the west coast?
questions.fact: The cliffs rise hundreds of metres from the sea. Boat trips go beneath them.

questions.q: On a booking, what does 'media pensión' mean?
a: Half board: breakfast and one other meal
A half-price room for each night
A room that has been booked for only half the night
A free half-day tour for guests
questions.fact: 'Pensión completa' is full board and 'todo incluido' is all inclusive.

questions.q: On a booking, what does 'vista al mar' mean?
questions.fact: 'Vista a la piscina' means pool view.

questions.q: What does a hotel's 'animación' team organise?
questions.fact: Think games, quizzes, shows and kids' clubs.

questions.q: Which season is peak time for UK visitors to Tenerife?
questions.fact: Winter is when the north of Europe wants sun. Tenerife's temperatures stay mild all year.

questions.q: About how high does the Teide cable car take you?
questions.fact: The top station is a short walk from the peak.

questions.q: To walk the last part to Teide's summit, what do you need?
a: A free permit, booked online in advance
A mountain guide from the park office
Nothing at all, just a good pair of boots
Oxygen tanks hired at the cable car
questions.fact: The permit limits numbers. Check the National Park website.

questions.q: Teide National Park is what?
a: A private nature reserve owned by a family
questions.fact: It is among the most visited national parks in Europe.

questions.q: Which rock near Teide's parador appeared on the old 1,000-peseta banknote?
questions.fact: Roque Nublo is on Gran Canaria.

questions.q: What makes the sky above Teide so special?
a: It is always covered by thick cloud
The sun never sets there in summer
Very clear, dark air and an international observatory
It has glowing aurora lights on most clear winter nights
questions.fact: Guided stargazing tours are popular.

questions.q: What is Masca?
a: A busy ferry port for La Gomera
A volcano crater near the summit
A tiny mountain village above a famous ravine
A famous black sand beach on the south east coast
questions.fact: Hiking the ravine to the sea normally needs a booked permit. Check the current rules.

questions.q: 'Loro' in Loro Parque means what?
questions.fact: The park started as a parrot sanctuary in Puerto de la Cruz.

questions.q: Siam Park near Costa Adeje is themed on which country?
questions.fact: It's one of the world's best-known water parks.

questions.q: Which Tenerife city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.fact: San Cristóbal de La Laguna is an old university town with colonial streets.

questions.q: What is the Drago Milenario at Icod de los Vinos?
a: A giant dragon statue in the square
A volcanic cave under the town
A stone pyramid on the hill
questions.fact: It is said to be centuries old. Its resin turns blood-red.

questions.q: Which explorer helped make the Güímar pyramids famous?
questions.fact: He believed ancient sailors crossed the Atlantic.

questions.q: What is the Cueva del Viento?
a: A wind farm on the ridge
A sea cave that you can reach by boat from the harbour
A bat sanctuary in the north
One of the world's longest lava tubes
questions.fact: Guided tours only. Book ahead.

questions.q: What is special about the Anaga mountains?
a: A ski slope that opens each winter
Ancient laurel forest and a Biosphere Reserve
A military base on the summit
A huge crater lake that you can swim in all year
questions.fact: Good hiking, and often misty and green.

questions.q: Which island can you see from the south coast, reached by ferry from Los Cristianos?
questions.fact: It's known for its whistled language, Silbo Gomero.

questions.q: Which Tenerife town lost its harbour in a 1706 eruption and now has lava rock pools?
questions.fact: The El Caletón pools are a favourite place to swim.

questions.q: The Santa Cruz carnival is often called the second biggest in the world after...?
questions.fact: It's held in February or March, with costumes, parades and street parties.

questions.q: What is the 'lucha canaria'?
questions.fact: It's one of the oldest sports of the islands.

questions.q: What is a timple?
a: A type of accordion used in folk music
A large drum that is carried through the streets
A small guitar-like instrument of the Canaries
A flute made of volcanic stone
questions.fact: It has five strings and is used in folk music.

questions.q: When is the Canary Islands Day (Día de Canarias)?
questions.fact: The island holds fiestas, folk music and traditional dress.

questions.q: Who designed the Auditorio de Tenerife in Santa Cruz?
questions.fact: The white building with a huge wing-like roof is a city landmark.

questions.q: What are 'romerías'?
a: Village pilgrimages with decorated carts and costume
Annual festivals when the fishermen bless their boats at sea
Auctions of the new season's wine
questions.fact: Fun to watch if you're visiting at the right time.

questions.q: What is the Silbo Gomero?
a: A type of goat's cheese from the island
A technique for fishing at night
A whistled language used on La Gomera
questions.fact: UNESCO recognises it as a cultural heritage.

questions.q: Who were the Guanches?
a: Spanish soldiers who arrived in the 1400s
Portuguese traders who settled in the south
questions.fact: They lived on the island until the Spanish conquest in the 1400s.

questions.q: When did Spain complete the conquest of Tenerife?
questions.fact: The Guanche kingdoms (menceyatos) fell to the Spanish in that decade.

questions.q: Which British admiral lost his arm attacking Santa Cruz in 1797?
questions.fact: The Spanish defenders won that battle.

questions.q: The statues beside Candelaria's basilica show who?
questions.fact: The patron saint of the Canaries is the Virgin of Candelaria, and pilgrims come on 15 August.

questions.q: What happens in La Orotava at Corpus Christi?
a: Streets are carpeted with flowers and coloured sand
A night-long fireworks battle between two neighbouring villages
A giant bull run through the old town
A boat parade with decorated yachts
questions.fact: The carpets are made overnight and trampled by processions.

questions.q: What is the Canarian accent like?
a: Almost exactly the same as Portuguese spoken in Lisbon
Closer to Latin American than mainland Spanish
Closer to Catalan than any other form of Spanish
Very close to Italian as spoken in Rome
questions.fact: Historic links across the Atlantic shaped it.

questions.q: What are the colours of the Canary Islands flag, left to right?
a: Red, yellow, red, with a crest in the middle
questions.fact: The flag is a vertical tricolour. Spain's is red, yellow, red.

questions.q: Tap Tenerife, where you are heading.
questions.fact: It's in the middle of the group, with Gran Canaria to the east and La Gomera to the west.

questions.q: Tap La Gomera, the island you reach by ferry from Los Cristianos.
questions.fact: The crossing takes about an hour.

questions.q: Tap Lanzarote, the island with the volcanic Timanfaya landscape.
questions.fact: César Manrique shaped much of its look.

questions.q: Tap Fuerteventura, known for its long sandy beaches and wind sports.
questions.fact: It is the Canary island closest to Africa.

questions.q: Tap Gran Canaria, home of the Maspalomas dunes.
questions.fact: Las Palmas, its capital, is the biggest city in the islands.

questions.q: Tap La Palma, where a volcano erupted in 2021.
questions.fact: The Cumbre Vieja eruption lasted nearly three months.

questions.q: Tap El Hierro, the smallest and westernmost of the main islands.
questions.fact: It once marked the end of the known world on old maps.

questions.q: Tap the Canary island closest to the African coast.
questions.fact: It's roughly 100 km from Morocco.

questions.q: Tap Mount Teide, in the middle of the island.
questions.fact: It rises out of a huge crater, and the cable car starts on its south-east side.

questions.q: Tap Santa Cruz, the capital, on the north-east coast.
questions.fact: A busy port with a carnival and a modern auditorium.

questions.q: Tap Puerto de la Cruz, the classic northern resort.
questions.fact: Home to Loro Parque and the Lago Martiánez pools.

questions.q: Tap Los Cristianos, the southern port with ferries to La Gomera.
questions.fact: It sits right next to Playa de las Américas.

questions.q: Tap Los Gigantes, below the great sea cliffs on the west coast.
questions.fact: Dolphins are often seen on boat trips from here.

questions.q: Tap Masca, the mountain village in the Teno mountains.
questions.fact: It sits above a deep ravine that leads to the sea.

questions.q: Tap El Médano, the windy south-east spot for windsurfing and kitesurfing.
questions.fact: Its beach and the Montaña Roja volcano cone are well known.

questions.q: Tap Garachico, the town with lava rock pools.
questions.fact: A 1706 eruption buried its harbour.

questions.q: Tap La Laguna, the UNESCO-listed university city.
questions.fact: It is just inland from Santa Cruz.

questions.q: Tap Costa Adeje, home of Siam Park.
questions.fact: One of the smartest parts of the south-west.

questions.q: Tap Playa de las Américas, the nightlife resort.
questions.fact: It was a fishing hamlet before it grew into a resort.

questions.q: Tap Anaga, the green mountain tip of the north-east.
questions.fact: It has ancient laurel forest and good walking.

questions.q: Tap Icod de los Vinos, home of the Drago Milenario.
questions.fact: The dragon tree is its best-known sight.

questions.q: Tap Candelaria, with its famous basilica and Guanche statues.
questions.fact: A pilgrimage town on the east coast.
